text:
Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. At eight months old, you've been experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension; can you describe exactly what happens during his meals and whether he vomits anything?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_XRay

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that clarification. Since there is no fever or diarrhea, have you noticed any specific stool changes, such as a greasy, foul smell or a "floating" quality that might suggest malabsorption? REQUEST TEST: Stool_Reduction_and_Elimination_Tests; REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_XRay

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the results. Since his stool is normal and he has no fever or diarrhea, have you noticed any difficulty passing gas or stool, and is his abdominal distension present immediately after feeding or only later? REQUEST TEST: Anorectal_Manometry; REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_XRay
